name: v5b
about: Opt-in sibling of v5 (select with ROBOLAB_BODY=v4 ROBOLAB_CALIB=v5b): the same source-based rectus femoris / hip flexor split as v5 (rf 80 N = 32 % of hip flexion, hip_flex_pos 170: hip flexion total 250 N m kept) but the vasti keep v4's value (knee_neg 230), so the knee-extension total is 294 N m (v4 and v5: 350) and the rectus femoris is 21.8 % of it (sources 15-22 %). Why it exists: in the anat5 A/B the champion's gears run on v5b with no retuning (gear 3 from gear-2 flying starts: 12/12 survive, steady 7.91 m/s, fold 110 deg, cadence 4.3/s; v4: 7.76 m/s, 96 deg, 4.16) while v5's stronger vasti (knee_neg 286: what makes up the knee total) makes the same stride fall (0/12): the controllers were tuned to the v4 vasti. The price is a 16 % weaker knee extension in total, which is the more conservative direction against v4.json's note that the model's capacities already exceed young men's voluntary maxima. A DIFFERENT BODY: not comparable with the v4 rows of the arena, nor with v5.

tendon_scale.unit: multiplier on the v3 quadriceps series stiffness (250 N/mm at 4.5 cm): 4.0 = 1000 N/mm
evidence: whole vasti series elasticity in OpenSim models, from the model files: ~976 N/mm (gait2392), ~927 N/mm (Rajagopal 2016)

patellar tendon stiffness in vivo: 1076 N/mm (O'Brien et al. 2010), 2826 (Helland et al. 2013), 3185-3269 (Bojsen-Moller et al. 2007), 3622 (Couppe et al. 2012), 4334 (Hansen et al. 2006); the whole muscle-tendon series (tendon plus aponeurosis) is more compliant than the free tendon, so the models' ~1000 N/mm is taken
Achilles kept at 200 N/mm (188 +- 43 in hopping, Lichtwark & Wilson 2005; 306-319, Rosager et al. 2002)

omega_muscle.unit: unloaded joint angular velocity of one muscle direction, rad/s (hip_flex_neg = hip extensors: gluteus maximus and, through their hip action, the hamstrings; hip_flex_pos = hip flexors: iliopsoas and, through its hip action, rectus femoris); MuJoCo vmax = omega * 0.3 / joint range
evidence: w0 = fibre vmax x optimal fibre length / moment arm with the standard models' fibre vmax of 10 L0/s (OpenSim Thelen2003 default, gait2392, Hamner 2010, Rajagopal 2016; Arnold & Delp 2011) and Ward et al. 2009's fibre lengths: PCSA-weighted hip extensors ~18.5 rad/s, hip flexors ~29 rad/s (at 15 L0/s, the high-speed models' value: ~28 and ~44); the standard 10 L0/s values are taken

the v3 value (15 for both) is below what sprinting needs: 79 sprinters at 9.9 m/s reach hip extension 850 +- 73 deg/s (14.8 rad/s) in stance and thigh lift 792 deg/s (13.8 rad/s) in swing (Miyashiro et al. 2019, PMC7739839), where a w0 of 15 leaves the muscles ~0 % of their force
omega_muscle.verified: derived (fibre vmax and fibre lengths verified in the model files and Ward 2009; hip moment arms typical values)

peaks.unit: unscaled peak isometric force / torque scale of one muscle direction (N m at coefficient 1); the population profile then multiplies it (p95: x1.32). hip_flex_pos = the lumped monoarticular hip flexors (iliopsoas, sartorius, tensor fasciae latae, pectineus, anterior adductors), knee_neg = the lumped vasti, rf = the biarticular rectus femoris (torque 1.0 x F at the hip, 0.8 x F at the knee). Both legs.

totals_kept.knee extension: NOT kept: knee_neg 230 + 0.8 x rf 80 = 294 N m (v4: 230 + 120 = 350; v5 makes it up with knee_neg 286)
totals_kept.unchanged: knee_neg (the vasti) 230, hip extension, knee flexion, ankle, toe, every speed / tendon / activation value

evidence: the sources' rectus femoris share of HIP FLEXION capacity (isometric F_max x sagittal moment arm, every muscle with a positive hip-flexion arm in the denominator; knee 90 deg): gait2392 (Delp 1990 lineage, model file gait2392_thelen2003muscle.osim) 19 / 26 / 29 / 31 / 30 % at hip -20 / 0 / 20 / 40 / 60 deg with iliopsoas 43 / 46 / 47 / 46 / 48 %; Rajagopal et al. 2016 (IEEE TBME 63:2068, Table II forces) 19 / 29 / 36 / 39 / 41 % with iliopsoas 32 / 29 / 28 / 30 / 34 %; Arnold et al. 2010 cadaver forces (Ann Biomed Eng 38:269, Table 1, PMC2903973) on the Rajagopal geometry 16 / 25 / 32 / 36 / 37 % with iliopsoas 33 / 31 / 31 / 33 / 37 %. A sprinter's swing runs the hip from about -20 to +60 deg flexion, so 26-41 % (about 32 % as the middle of the flexed-hip values) is the source share; 60 % is not (it is roughly the cadaver RF share among iliopsoas + RF ONLY, Kumazaki et al. 2022, 57-62 %, while v4's lumped hip flexor also holds sartorius, tensor fasciae latae, pectineus and the adductors)

the sources' rectus femoris share of KNEE EXTENSION capacity, RF / (RF + vasti), hip 0 deg, knee 0-120 deg: gait2392 19-22 %, Rajagopal 2016 19-21 %, Rajagopal-Lai-Uhlrich 2023 20-22 %, Arnold 2010 forces on the Rajagopal geometry 16-17 %; by force only 15.2 % (Arnold 2010: 848.8 N against 4723 N of vasti), 18.6 % (Rajagopal), 20.5 % (gait2392); by PCSA 15.7 % (Ward et al. 2009, Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074, PMC2650051: rectus femoris 13.5 cm2, vasti 35.1 + 16.7 + 20.6 cm2). In the models the vasti and the rectus femoris act through the same patellar tendon with similar knee-extension moment arms (rectus femoris 4.6-5.0 cm, vasti 4.0-4.9 cm at 0-30 deg knee flexion, gait2392 / Rajagopal), so the share of capacity is close to the share of force. 34 % is above every source

the compromise taken: rf 80 N, i.e. 32 % of hip flexion (sources 26-41 %) and 18.3 % of knee extension (sources 15-22 %); the two shares are tied by the fixed 1.0 : 0.8 coefficients, so one rf value cannot match a low knee share (cadaver PCSA 15 %) and Rajagopal's high hip share (38-41 %) together; 80 is inside both ranges. Alternatives priced in the split_check block: rf 66 (knee 15.1 %, hip 26.4 %), rf 88 (knee 20.1 %, hip 35.2 %)

the vasti keep v4's 230 (unlike v5): the anat5 A/B found the champion's strides tuned to the v4 vasti (any stronger knee_neg makes gear 3 fall: rf 110 / 140 / 262: 2/12 survive, 95 / 155 / 274: 0/12, v5: 0/12, while rf 80 / hip_flex_pos 170 / knee_neg 230: 12/12), and a lower knee-extension total is the conservative direction against v4.json's note (capacities already 1.4-2.9x young men's voluntary maxima); the rectus femoris' knee share 21.8 % is inside the sources' 15-22 %
peaks.verified: derived (as v5); the choice not to raise the vasti is an experimental finding, not a literature value

kept.everything else: every other parameter of v4.json (tendon_scale quadriceps x4, omega_muscle hip_flex_neg 18.5 / hip_flex_pos 29 rad/s) and every default of the v4 builder (peaks of all other muscles: hip_flex_neg 120, knee_pos 40, ankle 150 / 80, ham 200, gas 180; segments, foot contact, activation, force-length, force-velocity)
kept.rf coefficients: the rectus femoris keeps V2_BIARTICULAR's 1.0 (hip) : 0.8 (knee) coefficients (a code constant, not a calibration key)
kept.quadriceps tendon: the group's total series stiffness is unchanged; the v3 builder shares it among the group's muscles in proportion to their peak torques, so with the smaller rf the vasti's tendon is stiffer than in v4 (p95 XML: knee_neg 1996 -> 2376) and the rf's softer (1627 -> 1033): a consequence of the builder's sharing rule, not a separate choice

split_check.how: scratchpad/anat5/lit/{moment_arms.py, osim_paths.py, scenarios.py, moment_arms_*.json, shares.json, scenarios.json, tables.txt, sources.json}: muscle-tendon path lengths from the .osim path points, conditional / moving points, joint transforms and cylinder wraps, moment arm = -dL/dtheta by central differences (sagittal, pelvis fixed), capacity = F_max x arm; shares over every muscle with a positive hip-flexion arm (knee 90 deg for the hip table).
split_check.draft_rejected: the first proposal (rf 60, hip_flex_pos 190, knee_neg 302: 24 % of hip flexion, 13.7 % of knee extension) is below every source share on both joints (hip 26-41 %, knee 15-22 %); it was run only as a what-if through ROBOLAB_CALIB_SET (scratchpad/anat5/LOG.md) and is not a calibration

Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL. Are current measurements of lower extremity muscle architecture accurate? Jiroumaru T, et al. SpringerPlus 2014;3:624 (PMC4221557): isometric hip-flexion torque of 10 young men 159.7 N m at 0 deg (knee 90), 70 % at 30 deg, 50 % at 60 deg; the iliopsoas contribution is relatively larger in the flexed hip (qualitative)

IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 1990;37:757-767 lineage; Thelen, Seth, Anderson, Delp): iliacus 1073 N, psoas 1113, rectus femoris 1169, sartorius 156, TFL 233, pectineus 266, vasti 1294 + 1365 + 1871 N
sources.not accessible (nothing quoted from them: Delp 1990 and Arnold et al. 2000 (Comput Aided Surg 5:108) full texts, Nemeth & Ohlsen 1985, Visser et al. 1990, Spoor & van Leeuwen 1992, Herzog & Read 1993 (scanned), Handsfield et al. 2014 (paywalled): no hip-flexion moment-arm table could be re-read to validate the computed arms
sources.file_layer: scratchpad/anat5/lit/sources.json lists each source with its status

not_applied.posture-dependent rf knee coupling: the moment-arm ratio RF knee / RF hip is 0.36-0.54 in all three models at hip 40-60 deg and knee 90-120 deg (the fold-back posture) and 1.2-1.4 at hip 0, knee 30 deg (stance); V2_BIARTICULAR's fixed 0.8 therefore overstates the rectus femoris's knee-extension pull in the swing by ~1.5-2x. A fixed MuJoCo tendon cannot vary with posture; a lower constant coefficient would understate the stance; a code change, not a calibration key, so not part of v5
not_applied.sartorius / gracilis (hip flexion + knee: no biarticular hip-flexor-knee-flexor exists in the v2-v4 anatomy (sartorius 113-249 N, gracilis 162-281 N in the models: small); an optional v5.1 (needs a body.py change), not part of v5
